top_choice_rationale: Anne Carson (P001) remains my first choice on the common criteria. Her voice is exact, cool and sometimes comic, and it turns suddenly to desire or grief. Her formal invention is tied to specific emotional and intellectual problems: Autobiography of Red remakes the Geryon myth as a verse novel, and Nox makes elegy from a Catullus translation, glosses and fragments. Her long engagement with Greek and Latin literature works as method, not decoration. The citation, as the round-2 exchange narrowed it, credits original written work in English (lyric, verse narrative, essay) and treats translation, adaptation and scholarship as context, which answers the scope and book-object objections. My reservation is sustained quality: from public knowledge I cannot confirm that the mid-career and later books (Short Talks, The Beauty of the Husband, Red Doc>, Float) reach the level of the two landmark books. I have not read the full corpus or verified sources. I can judge her English directly and Romanian only in translation, which may inflate my confidence in her, and I count that only as less uncertainty, not as merit. The preference over Cărtărescu (P002) is narrow, and his sustained single project is a serious claim. The open question of development versus repetition cannot be settled from translations. P002 ranks above no award, since both leading claims meet the common criteria well enough to merit a prize. The count of supporters is not weighed as evidence.
recusal_note: none apparent from the profile; documented connections (co-election with David Håkansson, collaboration with Kate Larson, Lagerlöf research, service with committee colleagues) do not link to either shortlisted writer on the slate. I disclose that I am one of the explicit P001 supporters. Conflicts are disclosed and not adjudicated.
